$comment: C11/C23 6.4.5 (D-CSUBSET-WIDE-HEX-OCTAL-ESCAPE-VALUE, STRING half): a hex or octal escape in a wide/UTF string names a RAW CODE-UNIT VALUE and is assembled directly instead of being re-read as UTF-8. This example replaces a SILENT MISCOMPILE - u"\xC3\xA9" once collapsed through the UTF-8 re-decoder into one wrong 0x00E9 unit, and a wholesale refusal stood in for the fix for several cycles. Both are gone: the literal is TWO units, asserted by VALUE and by sizeof so the semantic tier's array length is pinned with it and the two tiers cannot disagree on N. The cases are chosen against the tempting wrong implementation (treat the escape as a code POINT and re-encode): u"\xD800" is a lone surrogate, U"\xFFFFFFFF" is past U+10FFFF, u"\777" is octal above 255, and u"\xF" "F" pins the phase-5-per-segment offset rebase. It also pins the ONE DELIBERATE DIVERGENCE FROM A REFERENCE: for a u8 string, gcc, clang, mingw-w64 and ISO C 6.4.5 make the escape ONE RAW BYTE while MSVC 19.51 UTF-8-encodes it as a code point (C3 BF, and C3 83 C2 A9). That split is on MEANING, so it was ruled rather than assumed - ISO C is a named vertex of the union and MSVC is the sole outlier - and the u8 arms exist so a later cycle applying the union by reflex cannot quietly flip it. Every value MEASURED 2026-09-02 on gcc 13.3.0, clang 18.1.3, mingw-w64 gcc 13.2.0 and MSVC 19.51, each compiled and RUN with its emitted units read back.

optimizedPipelines.label: release
optimizedPipelines.$comment: The code units are produced in phase 5 and reach the image as initialized read-only data, so the shipped pipeline has no literal-decoding work to transform and the image is expected to match the baseline. Deliberately NOT given mustDifferFromBaseline - an honest no-op. The arm earns its place by proving that constant folding over the unit values cannot re-derive a different answer from the one the front end assembled.
